name: Authored change → validate it with the OpenSpec CLI oracle
description:
The validate station. `validate` is a SUB-STEP of the OpenSpec lifecycle, not a coordinator taxonomy action, so no coordinator decision routes it — instead this rule chains off the authored marker. When an authoring loop calls create_change, the tool stamps openspec.change.authored=<slug> on THAT loop entity (the slug-independent signal; the run's own facts are slug-namespaced and no rule condition can wildcard-match them). This rule fires on that marker and spawns a validate loop that calls validate_change, which hydrates the change from the run's facts, shells `openspec validate <slug> --strict --json --no-interactive` in a temp dir, and — from the real exit code (G3) — stamps openspec.validated on the run (pass) or clears it (fail). The existing run-lifecycle/01-offer-change-approval gate then advances executing→awaiting_approval.

WHY the marker lives on the LOOP (not the run): this rule fires on the authoring loop entity, which carries agent.run (inherited via the create_change spawn's run_scope=inherit), so run_scope=inherit here propagates the SAME run to the validate loop — its validate_change call targets the run the change was authored on. A run entity carries no agent.run triple, so a run-fired rule could not inherit.

ROLE = coordinator (3-role roster; validate is a coordinator sub-step like authoring). tool_choice=function forces validate_change and tools stays nil (global discovery advertises it), so the validate loop runs the oracle and terminates (StopLoop) rather than deciding — it writes openspec.validated (not coordinator.decision.*), triggering no coordinator decision rule. Edge-triggered firing means the marker fires this exactly once; the validate loop carries no marker, so it does not re-fire.

No openspec.validated guard: the rule fires on the LOOP marker, and openspec.validated lives on the RUN — not readable from the firing loop entity. Edge-triggering (fire-once on the authoring loop) is the re-fire guard; a rework re-author is a NEW loop entity, a legitimate fresh trigger (D5/D15#0: a re-author re-validates).

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
SEMDEV — validate this run's authored OpenSpec change.

The change $entity.triple.openspec.change.authored has been authored onto the run. Validate it against the real OpenSpec CLI with the validate_change tool (pass the slug $entity.triple.openspec.change.authored). You supply only the slug — never a pass/fail; the harness reads the CLI's real exit code. Calling validate_change completes your turn.

metadata.station: validate — run the OpenSpec CLI oracle on the authored change
metadata.trigger: openspec.change.authored on the authoring loop entity (create-change-author-tool stamps it; slug-independent so a rule can match it).
metadata.run_scope_rationale: inherit — fires on the authoring LOOP (carries agent.run), so the validate loop inherits the same run the change was authored on. A run-entity-fired rule could not inherit (no agent.run there).
metadata.advances: openspec.validated on the run → run-lifecycle/01-offer-change-approval fires executing→awaiting_approval.
